title: Gâteau au Lard (Bacon Cake)
description: A cake made with bacon, bacon fat, and flour.

ingredients.name: three quarterons of small bacon, cut into very thin slices
ingredients.sourceText: three quarterons of small bacon, cut into very thin slices

ingredients.name: one and a half litrons of flour
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half litrons of flour

ingredients.name: bacon fat rendered from cooking the bacon
ingredients.sourceText: bacon fat rendered from cooking the bacon

steps: Cut three quarterons of small bacon into very thin slices
Put them in a saucepan over a low fire to cook for half an hour
Spread one and a half litrons of flour on a table and make a hole in the middle
Put in the rendered bacon fat from cooking the bacon, half a pound of butter, a little salt, and two eggs
Add one large glass of water and knead the dough
Let it rest for one hour
Distribute all the bacon slices throughout the dough, spacing them somewhat apart from each other
Form your cake in the usual way, glaze with beaten egg
Bake for a good hour in the oven or under a pie-dish cover

title: Gâteau au Riz (Rice Cake)
description: A cake made with rice, cream, and lemon.
steps: Boil one pint of cream
Add half-pound of sugar and three quarterons of rice
When the rice bursts, melt a quarter-pound of butter into it
Mince the zest of a lemon and add it
When the rice is cold, add four whole eggs and four yolks (more if the rice is thick)
Butter a mold and line it with breadcrumbs, then invert so only a thin coating remains
After half an hour, before serving, put the rice in the mold
Place it on red ash and surround it with a cover on top filled with fire
The mold must not be full lest the rice overflow as it swells
At the moment of service, unmold onto the plate and take care to detach the edges
If you wish to make a soufflé, whip six egg whites as for other soufflés and mix them with the rice, pouring into a small silver saucepan

title: Gâteau de Brioche (Brioche Cake)
description: A cake made with yeast or bread, flour, and water.

ingredients.name: more than half an ounce of brewer's yeast or a small piece of bread yeast
ingredients.sourceText: more than half an ounce of brewer's yeast or a small piece of bread yeast

ingredients.name: one and a half pounds of butter
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half pounds of butter

ingredients.name: nearly one ounce of fine salt
ingredients.sourceText: nearly one ounce of fine salt

steps: Put one litron of flour on a table and knead it with a little warm water and more than half an ounce of brewer's yeast, or if you do not have it, a small piece of bread yeast in its place
Wrap this paste in a cloth and let it rise in a warm place for a quarter hour in summer and one hour in winter
Then put two litrons of flour on a table with the paste you have made as leaven, one and a half pounds of butter, ten eggs, half a glass of water, and nearly one ounce of fine salt
Knead everything together with the palm of your hands three times
Dust with flour and wrap in a cloth, letting it rise for nine or ten hours
Cut this paste according to the size of brioche cakes you want to make
Moisten them by rounding them with your hands and flatten the top slightly
Glaze with beaten egg
Bake in the oven for half an hour for small ones and one and a half hours for large ones

title: Gâteau de Riz (Rice Cake)
description: A cake made with rice, water, and milk.

ingredients.name: a little more than a quarteron of well-washed rice
ingredients.sourceText: a little more than a quarteron of well-washed rice

steps: Put in a small pot a little more than a quarteron of well-washed rice
Make it burst over the fire with a glass of water, and then add good milk until it is well cooked and thick

Make a paste with one litron of flour, salt, four eggs, half a pound of butter, and the rice
Knead everything together and form a cake
Glaze with beaten egg
Bake in the oven for one hour, or under a pie-dish cover, taking care to butter the paper that you put under the cake

title: Gâteau de Savoie (Savoy Cake)
description: A cake made with orange, eggs, and sugar.

ingredients.name: fine sugar in weight equal to fourteen eggs
ingredients.sourceText: fine sugar in weight equal to fourteen eggs

ingredients.name: flour in weight equal to seven eggs
ingredients.sourceText: flour in weight equal to seven eggs

steps: Weigh fourteen eggs on a balance
On the other side put fine sugar equal in weight
Remove the sugar and put flour in its place, weighing the amount of seven eggs
Set the flour aside
Break the eggs, putting the yolks in one bowl and the whites in another
With the yolks put the sugar you have weighed, a little grated green lemon zest, and grilled and chopped orange flower
Beat everything together for half an hour
Then add the well-beaten egg whites and the flour you have weighed, adding it gently while stirring the batter with a whisk
Get a medium-sized and deep saucepan or cake mold that you first rub with refined butter, wipe it well with a cloth and coat with refined butter so it spreads everywhere
Put your batter in and bake in the oven with moderate heat for a good hour and a half
When cooked, turn it out gently onto a platter
If it is a beautiful golden color, serve it natural
If it has too much color, glaze it with white icing made with very fine sugar, one egg white, and the juice of half a lemon
Beat everything together in a faience dish with a wooden spoon until the icing is very white
Use it to cover the whole cake and serve only when the icing is dry

title: Gâteau à la Crème (Cream Cake)
description: A cake made with double cream, flour, and salt.

Beat it five times like puff pastry dough
Form into one large cake or several small ones
Glaze with beaten egg and bake in the oven
You can use this proportion to make as many cakes as you wish

title: Gâteau à la Royale (Royal Cake)
description: A cake made with lemon, candied orange, and almond.

ingredients.name: a pinch of chopped green lemon
ingredients.sourceText: a pinch of chopped green lemon

ingredients.name: butter the size of half an egg
ingredients.sourceText: butter the size of half an egg

ingredients.name: four or five spoonfuls of flour
ingredients.sourceText: four or five spoonfuls of flour

steps: Put in a saucepan a pinch of chopped green lemon, {{source-1}}, a little salt, butter the size of half an egg, and a good glass of water
Bring to a boil for a moment and add four or five spoonfuls of flour
Dry out over the fire, stirring constantly until the paste is very thick and begins to stick to the saucepan
Remove from the fire and add one egg at a time, stirring vigorously with the spoon until it is well mixed with the paste
Continue adding eggs one by one in this manner until the paste is soft without being liquid
Add a little candied orange flowers and two bitter almond biscuits, finely ground, to the paste
Form small cakes the size of half an egg on buttered paper
Glaze the top with beaten egg
Bake for half an hour in the oven at a gentle heat

title: Gâteau à la Viande (Meat Cake)
description: A cake made with meat or hare or rabbit or beef or mutton, beef fat, and lard.

ingredients.name: meat (such as hare, rabbit, beef, or mutton)
ingredients.sourceText: meat (such as hare, rabbit, beef, or mutton)

ingredients.name: lard cut into dice
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of lard cut into dice

steps: Choose the meat that will give the name to your cake, such as hare cake, rabbit cake, beef cake, etc. All are made the same way, except that game is mixed with an equal amount of butcher's meat
For a mutton cake, take a leg, remove all the meat after removing the skin, and chop it with a little beef fat
Mix this meat with {{source-2}}, ten egg yolks, fine salt, fine spices, half a glass of brandy, mushrooms, a little shallots, parsley, and chives, all chopped
Put lard slices at the bottom of a saucepan and your meat farce on top after mixing it well with all its seasoning
Cook in the oven for at least three hours
When cooked, let it cool in the saucepan, then remove it to turn it out onto a plate
Leave the lard slices that are around the cake and rasp them lightly with a knife
Serve on a plate garnished with a napkin

title: Hachis de Bœuf (Chopped Beef Hash)
description: Prepared with beef, onions, and bouillon.
steps: Mince three or four onions very fine and put them in a casserole with a little butter
Cook over the fire until they are almost cooked
Add a good pinch of flour and stir until it is golden in color
Moisten with bouillon and half a glass of wine, season with salt and coarse pepper
Let boil until the onion is cooked and there is no more sauce
Add chopped beef and boil it so it takes on the taste of the onion
When serving, add a spoonful of mustard or a dash of vinegar

title: Hachis de Lapereau (Minced Young Rabbit)
description: Prepared with rabbits and eggs.
steps: Roast four young rabbits on the spit
When cooked and cold, remove the fillets and the largest part of the thighs
Remove the nerves and skin
Mince all the meat, neither too fine nor too coarse
Place the minced meat in a casserole with two or three spoonfuls of hot béchamelle
Mix the béchamelle with the minced meat; it should not be too thin
Keep it warm in a bain-marie
Arrange croutons around the dish
At the moment of serving, place the minced meat in the center
You may place poached eggs around it and small larded, glazed fillets between the eggs
If you do not have béchamelle, reduce velouté into which you put a liaison of three egg yolks

title: Hachis de Perdreaux (Partridge Hash)
description: Prepared with partridges, bay leaf, and shallots.
steps: Spit-roast 8 partridges; when cooked, let them cool
Remove the fillets and chop them; place in a saucepan
Make a light roux and add the livers and lungs of your partridges, 1 bay leaf, 1 clove, 3 shallots, and a little sage
Brown the whole with your roux; add 2 large glasses of bouillon
Reduce the sauce to half; strain it through fine cloth without pressing
Add sauce to your hash until it is thick and bound; keep it warm without boiling
At service, arrange croutons around your platter and put your hash in the center
Add around it soft-boiled eggs or poached eggs, placing a round crouton fried in oil between each egg

title: Haricot de Mouton (Lamb Stew)
description: Prepared with lamb shoulder, bouillon or water, and chives.
steps: Cut a lamb shoulder into pieces the width of two fingers and a bit longer
Make a roux with little butter and a spoonful of flour
Brown it on a small fire, stirring always with a spoon, until it is a dark cinnamon color
Add the meat and pass it over the fire five or six times, stirring from time to time
Add bouillon (or about a pint of warm water if no bouillon), little at a time so the roux can dissolve well, stirring always with the spoon until all is added
Season the meat with salt and pepper, a bouquet of parsley, chives, a bay leaf, thyme, basil, three cloves, and a clove of garlic
Cook on a small fire
Halfway through cooking, tilt the casserole so the fat comes to the top; remove it with a spoon
Add turnips cut into pieces and a bouquet
Tilt the casserole again to remove the remaining fat
When done, the sauce should be neither too clear nor too thick, that is to say of medium consistency
Dress your pieces in the serving dish, pour the sauce over them, and sprinkle with chopped parsley

title: Horly de Poulets (Chicken Horly)
description: Prepared with fat, scallions, and bay leaves.
steps: Singe and butcher the two chickens as you would for a fricassée and place the pieces in a vessel.
Season the chicken pieces with salt, coarse pepper, a pinch of parsley leaves, some broken scallions, two bay leaves, and the juice of two lemons.
Toss the chicken pieces in this seasoning.
Peel a dozen large onions of equal size and cut them into slices of equal thickness to form rings, discarding the centers.
Half an hour before serving, drain the chicken pieces and dust them with flour.
Toss them in a cloth and shake them well.
Place them in oil that is not too hot.
When they have a beautiful color and you judge them cooked, drain them on white cloth.
Heat your oil well.
Dust the onion rings with flour, toss them in a cloth, and place them in very hot oil.
When they have a beautiful color, drain them on white cloth.
Arrange the chicken pieces in a mound on a platter.
Place the onions on top and hot aspic underneath.

title: Hure de Cochon (Pork Head Cheese)
description: Prepared with pork, peppercorns, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Pork meat, fresh, fatty and lean
ingredients.sourceText: Pork meat, fresh, fatty and lean

ingredients.name: Seven to eight sprigs of thyme
ingredients.sourceText: Seven to eight sprigs of thyme

steps: Bone the head entirely; take pieces of fresh pork meat, fatty and lean, that you put with your head
Season it with salt, peppercorns, pounded aromatic herbs, four spices, chopped parsley and chives; let it sit in a vessel for eight or ten days

When it has well absorbed the seasoning, drain it; gather all your pieces lengthwise in your head, such as the tongue, the fillets, the pieces of lard that you cut lengthwise; arrange them so that your head is filled, and regains its original form
With a trussing needle and string sew the opening where you have boned it, and tie it with string so that in cooking it does not deform; wrap it in white linen that you tie at both ends

Then place it in a braising pan with the bones of your head, some rinds, eight to ten carrots, ten onions, eight bay leaves, seven or eight sprigs of thyme, basil, a large bouquet of parsley and chives, six cloves, a large handful of salt, and some pork scraps if you have any, or other meat
Moisten your head cheese with water until it is covered; braise it eight to ten hours over a gentle fire
Test it before to see if it is cooked; and if your larding needle has difficulty entering, it is not cooked

When you remove it from the fire, leave your head cheese two hours in its cooking liquid; then remove it with another white cloth; press it with your two hands, always keeping its form, but only to extract any liquid that remained in it
Let it cool in its cloth: when it is quite cold, unwrap it, prepare it, and place it on a folded napkin on a plate; be careful to remove the strings attached to it
You may also chop the meats inside; but the head cheese is more generally esteemed this way: the pieces are more whole, the interior more marbled

title: Jus (Gravy)
description: A sauce made with beef, rabbits, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Two rabbits, that is the hind legs and saddle only
ingredients.sourceText: Two rabbits, that is the hind legs and saddle only

ingredients.name: A bouquet of parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: A bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: Put in a saucepan {{source-0}}, two rabbits (that is to say the hind legs and the saddle, not the breast nor the head), one calf knuckle, five carrots, six onions, two cloves, two bay leaves, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Put two spoonfuls of broth in your saucepan which you place on a good fire
When the broth is reduced, smother your stove and put your saucepan on it so that your meat releases its jus and it attaches very gently
The glaze at the bottom of your saucepan must be almost black
When it reaches this point, take your saucepan from the fire and wait ten minutes without moistening it
Fill it with great broth or water, but in a lesser quantity
Then let your jus simmer for three hours on the fire
Let it be well skimmed and seasoned; if you moisten with water the cooked meats, pass your jus through a hair sieve

You can also make it with meat scraps: cut slices of onions that you put at the bottom of your saucepan, your meat on top (and the seasoning of the jus above), put two or three glasses of water; reduce it as the jus: when the bottom of your saucepan is almost black, fill it almost with water according to the quantity of meat; add the salt needed and let your jus boil for two hours; after pass it through the hair sieve

description: Prepared with rabbits, bacon, and saffron or turmeric.

ingredients.name: Two young rabbits, cut into equal pieces

ingredients.name: small bacon, cut into small square flat pieces

steps: Cut two young rabbits into equal pieces
In a casserole, heat three-quarters pound of butter
Add one pound of small bacon cut into small square flat pieces and brown it in the butter
Add {{source-3}}
Add ten small hot peppers pounded with a little salt
Add two bay leaves and two cloves
Once all the seasoning is well browned in the butter, add the rabbit pieces, which should be well dried to prevent blood
Remove the lungs
Brown the rabbit well
When the pieces are firm, add three spoonfuls of flour and mix well with the ragout
Moisten with bouillon or water
Add salt; there must be plenty of liquid so it can cook on high heat and reduce
Add mushrooms
When three-quarters cooked, add small onions, artichoke hearts if available, and eggplants
In India, all sorts of vegetables are added: haricots verts, cauliflower, tomatoes, cucumbers, etc.
When the curry is cooked, it must be swimming in sauce and fat; consequently, do not degrease it
You can serve it in this state, or if you wish, remove the meat and garnish and place them in the dish for serving
Make a liaison of five or six eggs in the sauce
Stir the sauce over the fire without letting it boil, as it would break
When thickened, pass it through a sieve over the ragout
Check that it is well spiced and well seasoned
Serve with rice bread in water alongside the curry dish, as the person serving the ragout places rice bread on the plate

steps: Cut and prepare your tendons as in the blanc method
Put butter, saffron or turmeric powder, small hot pepper, salt pork cut in flat squares, and bay leaves in a pot
Sauté your tendons with butter and pepper until well browned
Add four spoonfuls of flour and mix with the tendons and butter
Moisten the tendons with bouillon; there should be plenty of sauce
Add mushrooms and two cloves stuck in an onion, which you will remove when the curry is cooked
When the ragoût is half cooked, add artichoke bottoms that are three-quarters cooked and small onions
Do not degrease this ragoût because of its richness
For the rice bread: wash one and a half pounds of rice in five or six warm waters
Bring water to a boil in a pot; put the rice in to blanch for ten minutes
Drain on a sieve
Butter a pot of the right size to hold the rice; fill it with rice
Put it on a gentle heat with fire on the lid and around it so the rice dries, forms into bread, and takes color

At the moment of serving, pour the ragoût into a deep dish such as a tureen or salad bowl; turn over the rice bread and place on a plate beside the curry, as rice is placed on the plate where curry is served
If you do not have bouillon to moisten the curry, use water; then add salt, pepper, and a little grated nutmeg
The curry must be very yellow
Put nothing in the rice

title: Kari à la Française (French-Style Curry)
description: Prepared with veal and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: All ingredients as in Indian-style curry
ingredients.sourceText: All ingredients as in Indian-style curry

steps: Prepare your tendons and make the curry the same as the previous recipe
At the moment of serving, remove the meat and garnishes from your curry
Make sure it is very rich and the sauce is well bound and abundant
Make a liaison of five or six egg yolks according to the quantity of sauce
Bind your sauce on the heat, constantly stirring without letting it boil
When you see the sauce coat your spoon, pass it through a sieve over your curry
The meat and garnishes must bathe in the sauce, and the pepper must dominate
Season well with salt
If your sauce is too thin, add some velouté

title: Lamb Chops à la Pocheé (Poached Lamb Chops)
description: Prepared with lamb, shallots, and bouillon.
steps: Take a rack of aged lamb, cut it by ribs, and put them in a saucepan with a piece of good butter
Cook them over a small fire, turning them from time to time, until they are completely cooked
Remove them from the saucepan to drain of their fat
Leave about half a spoonful of fat in the same saucepan and add a glass of bouillon, chopped shallots, salt, and coarse pepper
Bring to a boil to loosen what sticks to the saucepan
Put the chops back in with three egg yolks
Bind the sauce over the fire without boiling
When serving, add a little nutmeg and a dash of vinegar

title: Lamb Tails with Cabbage, Bourgeoise Style (Queues de Mouton aux Choux, à la Bourgeoise)
description: Prepared with lamb, bouillon, and chives.

ingredients.name: half a large head of cabbage
ingredients.sourceText: half a large head of cabbage

ingredients.name: quarter pound of small lard or half a pound
ingredients.sourceText: quarter pound of small lard or half a pound

steps: Cook five or six lamb tails in a light braise made with a little bouillon, little salt, pepper, a bouquet of parsley, chives, two cloves, and half a clove of garlic.
Blanch half a large head of cabbage for a quarter hour in boiling water, then remove to fresh water and press it.
Remove the core and chop the cabbage.
Cut a quarter pound of small lard or half a pound into small dice.
Mix the lard and cabbage together in a roux made with a good pinch of flour and butter.
Pass them together and moisten with a little bouillon without salt.
Let cook for an hour over low heat until the cabbage and lard are well cooked and the ragout is well bound.
Drain the tails and wipe them with a cloth.
Arrange them in the dish at a small distance from one another.
Cover each tail with ragout and serve hot.

title: Lamb Tails with Rice (Queues de Mouton au Riz)
description: Prepared with lamb, bouillon, and chives.
steps: Cook the lamb tails with bouillon, a bouquet of parsley, chives, two cloves, half a clove of garlic, half a bay leaf, thyme, basil, salt, and pepper over low heat.
Remove from heat and let drain and cool.
Wash {{source-11}} several times in lukewarm water, rubbing it with your hands.
Put the rice in a small pot with the bouillon used to cook the tails, strained through a sieve without removing the fat; if there is not enough bouillon, add more.
Cook the rice over low heat; it should remain quite thick without being overcooked.
When half cold, cover the bottom of the serving dish with a little rice and arrange the tails on top so they do not touch.
Cover them completely with the remaining rice, preserving the shape of each tail.
Glaze the top lightly with beaten egg yolk.
Place the dish on a bed of hot ashes with a tourte lid covered with good fire.
Let cook until the tails are a golden color and the rice forms a crust.
Tilt the dish slightly to drain the fat, wipe the edges, and serve.

title: Lamb Tails à la Prussienne (Queues de Mouton à la Prussienne)
description: Prepared with lamb, cabbage, and lard.

ingredients.name: half a pound of small lard
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of small lard

steps: Blanch the lamb tails, cabbage, and small lard for a quarter hour in boiling water, then remove to fresh water.
Press the cabbage and cut it into several pieces, tying each separately.
Cut the small lard into several pieces without separating them from the rind, and tie them.
Place the tails at the bottom of a small pot, then add the cabbage, lard, and six large onions.
Add a bouquet of parsley, chives, two cloves, half a clove of garlic, a very small branch of fennel, salt, and coarse pepper.
Cover with bouillon and cook over low heat in a braise.
Cut bread crumbs into rounds the size of a small coin and pass them over the fire with butter until they are a beautiful golden color; set aside to toast.
Make a roux with a good pinch of flour in the remaining butter from the croutons and brown it.
Moisten with bouillon from the cooking of the cabbage and a dash of vinegar; boil for half an hour so the flour cooks and forms a light coulis to your taste.
Degrease and strain the sauce through a sieve.
When the tails are cooked and no sauce remains, drain them and wipe with a cloth.
Arrange the tails interspersed with the cabbage, onions around them, the lard and croutons on top of the cabbage.
Serve the sauce on top.

title: Langue de Bœuf en Atelet (Beef Tongue on Skewers)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, sauce, and breadcrumbs.
steps: When your tongue is cooked as described for cornichons, allow it to cool
Cut it into small thin squares
Place the pieces on a plate
Reduce Italian sauce until well reduced
When well reduced, add a short liaison of two or three eggs
Stir carefully so the sauce does not break
When the sauce is bound, pour it over the small squares of tongue and allow the sauce to cool
Ensure the tongue is well covered with sauce
Skewer each small piece with an atelet, ensuring the pieces are thoroughly coated with sauce
Make sure all pieces are the same size so the atelet presents a long square with four equal angles
Fill any gaps with sauce, smoothing the atelet
Dip it in warm butter
Roll it in breadcrumbs, then in beaten eggs mixed with a little butter, salt and coarse pepper
Bread it while maintaining its square shape
Grill it on three sides, browning the fourth side with a camp oven or ice shovel
If you lack Italian sauce, use hachée sauce instead

title: Langue à l'Écarlate (Scarlet Tongue)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, saltpeter, and bay leaf.
steps: Pound {{source-1}}
Rub the beef tongue thoroughly all over with the pounded saltpeter
Place the tongue in a terrine with thyme, bay leaf, basil, and peppercorns
Dissolve two large handfuls of salt in boiling water
When the salt is dissolved and the water is cold, pour it over the tongue
Leave the tongue in the brine for five or six days or longer
If you have time, soak the tongue for two hours before cooking
Blanch the tongue
Place it in a braise pan with a quarter of the brine, thyme, bay leaf, basil, peppercorns, two carrots, two onions, three cloves, two pints of water, and salt
Simmer gently for two hours
Remove from heat and allow to cool in its seasoning

Serve the grilled tongues with this piquant sauce

title: Lapereau au Blanc (Young Rabbit in White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with rabbit, bouillon, and mushrooms.
steps: Skin your young rabbit and gut it
Cut it into pieces like the previous recipe
Remove the liver and lungs
Wipe the pieces well so there is no blood, otherwise you would need to blanch it and that causes it to lose flavor
Put a quarter pound of butter in a casserole
Warm it and put your young rabbit inside
Brown it over high heat
When you see that all your pieces are stiffened, pour in two tablespoons of flour that you mix with your butter and rabbit
Add four tablespoons of bouillon
Stir your stew well until it boils

Add mushrooms that you have sautéed in water and lemon, a bouquet of parsley and chives, a bay leaf, a little thyme, a little pepper, and about half a pound of bacon that you have cut into small pieces

Put in a saucepan lard about the size of an egg, twice as much butter, and two spoonfuls of oil
Wipe your rabbit pieces well to remove the blood
Melt the butter and put the rabbit in it
Brown it well
Add chopped mushrooms, shallot, finely chopped parsley, salt, coarse pepper, a little ground aromatic spices, and grated nutmeg
Stir everything together on the fire
When the young rabbit has stayed ten minutes on the fire, take a strong double paper case which you oil
Put in the bottom a very thin lard strip, and place your rabbit pieces with all their seasoning, another thin lard strip over the top
At the moment of serving, place your case on the grill over gentle fire and place a hot camp oven over it
When serving, either add a little Italian sauce inside your case, or before putting it on the fire, mask it with breadcrumb and brown it with the oven

description: A bread preparation made with rabbits, lard, and butter or beef marrow.
steps: Skin and empty one or two young rabbits
Chop the livers to make a forcemeat with scraped lard, a little butter or beef marrow, chopped parsley, chives, and savory, salt, and coarse pepper
Bind this forcemeat with three egg yolks and put it inside the rabbit body, sewing it closed
Cook them on the coals
Cut strips of breadcrumbs the length of the rabbits with as many strips of small lard, well interlarded
Cover the entire body of the rabbits with these strips, alternating bread and lard so only the head of the rabbits shows
Wrap them with two sheets of well-buttered paper and cook slowly on the spit
When cooked and the bread slightly browned, remove the paper and serve with the bread strips, small lard, and the cooking juices to which you add a dash of verjuice

ingredients.name: A half glass of white wine
ingredients.sourceText: A half glass of white wine

steps: Cut the rabbits into pieces and cook them with a half glass of white wine, broth, a bouquet garni, salt, and coarse pepper
When they are cooked, reduce the sauce so that it attaches to the meat
Let cool
Thread them onto small skewers
Dip them in beaten egg
Bread them and dip them in fat again to bread them a second time
Grill them until they are a beautiful color
Serve dry with the skewers.

title: Lapereaux en Tortue (Young Rabbits Shaped as Turtle)
description: Prepared with rabbit, white wine, and bouillon.
steps: Empty a rabbit, leave the liver and remove the bitter part
Debone the rabbit only in the middle of the belly
Make a hole in the skin to pass the front half of the rabbit through it so it becomes inverted and takes the shape of a turtle
Tie it and cook with a glass of white wine, a little bouillon, a bouquet of parsley, chives, a garlic clove, two cloves, thyme, bay leaf, basil, salt, and pepper
When cooked, pass the sauce through a sieve, degrease it, and add a little coulis to bind it
Reduce to sauce consistency and serve over the rabbit

title: Lapereaux Roulés aux Pistaches (Young Rabbits Rolled with Pistachios)
description: Prepared with rabbits, pistachios, and meat.
steps: Debone one or two young rabbits
Make a forcemeat from their livers with some other cooked meat, breadcrumbs passed through milk, parsley, chives, mushrooms, salt, and pepper
Bind the forcemeat with four egg yolks
Spread this forcemeat on the rabbits, roll them, and tie with string
Cook them with a little white wine, bouillon, and bouquet garni
When cooked, degrease the sauce and pass through a sieve
Add a little coulis to bind it and reduce to sauce consistency
When serving on the rabbits, add about twenty blanched pistachios

title: Lapin en Galantine (Rabbit Galantine)
description: Prepared with rabbit, rabbits, and lard.

ingredients.name: One rabbit, boned except for the head
ingredients.sourceText: One rabbit, boned except for the head

ingredients.name: Flesh from the thighs of the rabbit
ingredients.sourceText: Flesh from the thighs of the rabbit

ingredients.name: Lard, equal amount to the meat
ingredients.sourceText: Lard, equal amount to the meat

steps: Bone the rabbit, except for the head
Remove the largest part of the flesh from the thighs to make room for stuffing
Lard the flesh with medium-sized lardons seasoned
Mince the flesh from the thighs and fillets of two other rabbits
Add an equal amount of lard and mince everything together
Add salt, coarse pepper, a little pounded aromatic herbs, and chopped truffles
Once the forcemeat is made, lay out the rabbit and season it
Put a layer of forcemeat on it, then add lardons of scarlet tongue, pieces of truffles, and lardons
Add another layer of forcemeat, continuing in this manner
Once the rabbit is well filled, give it its original shape
Cover it with slices of bacon
Tie it with string and wrap it in white linen, which you will tie again
Place slices of bacon in a braising pan
Place the rabbit in it along with a veal knuckle cut into pieces and the debris from your rabbits

title: Lapin en Gibelotte (Rabbit Stew)
description: Prepared with rabbit, white wine, and bouillon.
steps: Cut your rabbit into pieces of equal size so they cook evenly
Put a quarter pound of butter in a casserole with two tablespoons of flour
Make a roux; when well browned, add the rabbit pieces to brown
Add half a bottle of white wine and about a bottle of bouillon
Stir your stew well until it boils
Add mushrooms, bacon that you have browned separately in a casserole, a bouquet of parsley and chives with some thyme and a bay leaf
Cook your stew over high heat so the braising liquid reduces
Add very little salt and some pepper
When three-quarters cooked, if desired, add eel sections and thirty small peeled onions that you have sautéed in butter over moderately high heat until well browned
Add the onions and eel at the same time
Take care to degrease your stew
Your sauce should be neither too thick nor too thin
Check that the seasoning is good
Remove the bouquet and serve your stew

title: Lapin en Matelote (Rabbit Sailor Style)
description: Prepared with rabbit, red wine, and bouillon.
steps: Cut a rabbit into pieces
Make a small roux with one small spoonful of flour and a piece of butter
Put the rabbit pieces with the liver in it, pass them over the fire and moisten with one glass of red wine, two glasses of water and bouillon
Add a bouquet of parsley, chives, one garlic clove, two cloves, thyme, bay leaf, basil, salt, coarse pepper
Cook over low heat; half an hour later add a dozen blanched small onions
If you wish to add an eel cut into sections, add it only when the rabbit is three-quarters cooked
Before serving, remove the bouquet, degrease the sauce and add a good handful of whole capers and one chopped anchovy
Serve with croutons fried in butter; pour the sauce over all

title: Lapin Farci Glacé (Stuffed Glazed Rabbit)
description: Prepared with rabbit, lard, and truffles.
steps: Chop together more lard than meat; add salt, coarse pepper, a little ground aromatic spices, and chopped truffles
Extend the rabbit and season it; place a layer of stuffing, and over it lardons of scarlet tongue, pieces of truffles, and lardons
Place another layer of stuffing and continue thus
Once the rabbit is well filled, give it its original form, cover it with lard strips, tie it, and wrap it in white linen, tying it again

Place lard strips in a braising pan; put your rabbit in it with the calf knuckle cut in pieces along with rabbit trimmings, two carrots, three onions (one studded with two cloves), two bay leaves, a little thyme, a bouquet of parsley and chives, half a bottle of white wine, one spoonful of bouillon, and a little salt
Simmer your rabbit for two hours over very low heat
When cooked, remove the braising pan from the fire; after half an hour, carefully remove your rabbit without breaking it
Let it cool in its linen
Serve it glazed or with breadcrumb coating
If you need aspic for decoration, pass the cooking liquid through a cloth, clarify it like aspic, let the aspic cool, and serve it with your rabbit

description: Prepared with rabbits, bouillon, and lard.

description: Prepared with leg of mutton, lard, and chives.
steps: Cut the leg of mutton lengthwise into slices about two fingers thick
Make four pieces from the leg
Lard all pieces with lard seasoned with parsley, chives, mushroom, a pinch of garlic, all chopped; salt and pepper
Line a casserole with a few strips of lard and slices of onions

Cover the casserole well and cook over very low heat in its own juice

When cooked, remove the fat from the sauce
If you have coulis, add a little to the sauce and serve with reduced sauce

title: Leg of Mutton in Water (Gigot de mouton à l'eau)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, broth, and chives.

ingredients.name: lard and anchovy fillets (optional for larding)
ingredients.sourceText: lard and anchovy fillets (optional for larding)

steps: Trim the shank of the leg by cutting the end so it is not so long
Lard the meat if desired with lard and some anchovy fillets; if you leave it without, tie it with string
Place it in a pot just fitted to its size with one chopine of water and as much broth
Bring to a boil and skim
Add a bouquet of parsley, chives, half a clove of garlic, three shallots, two cloves, two onions, one carrot, and one parsnip
When the leg is cooked, pass the broth through a sieve and remove the fat
Place it on the fire to reduce it until it becomes a glaze like a fricandeau
Put this glaze on top of the leg
Then put a few spoonfuls of broth in the pot to detach what remains
If you have some coulis, use it in place of the broth
Pass it through a sieve and serve under the leg

description: Prepared with leg of mutton, vinegar, and butter.
steps: Cook the leg in the same manner as the English style

title: Leg of Mutton à l'Anglaise (English Style)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, lard, and broth.
steps: Cut the shank and skin a little on the joint bone so you can bend the shank without disfiguring the leg
Lard the whole leg across with coarse lard
Tie the leg and place it in a pot just fitted to its size with broth, a bouquet of parsley, chives, one good clove of garlic, three cloves, one bay leaf, thyme, basil, salt, and pepper

For the sauce: put one glass of broth and nearly as much coulis in a casserole, with capers, one anchovy, a little parsley, chives, one shallot, and one hard egg yolk, all chopped very fine
Boil for two or three minutes
Serve on the leg

title: Levraut au Sang (Young Hare in Blood Sauce)
description: A sauce made with hare, chives, and garlic.

steps: When plucking and cleaning a young hare, be careful not to lose the blood; set it aside
Cut the hare into pieces and lard with coarse lard if desired
Put it in a saucepan with the liver and butter the size of an egg, a bouquet of parsley, chives, one garlic clove, two shallots, three cloves, one bay leaf, thyme, basil
Pass over the fire and add a good pinch of flour
Moisten with three glasses of bouillon, one half-setier of red wine, one spoonful of vinegar, salt, coarse pepper
Let boil until the young hare is cooked and a little sauce remains
Take the cooked liver, crush it well and mix with the blood you kept
When ready to serve, add the blood to make it bind on the fire without boiling, like an egg yolk liaison
Then add a half-handful of whole fine capers
Serve hot

title: Lièvre en Haricot (Hare Stew)
description: Prepared with hare, chives, and shallots.
steps: Skin and empty a hare, keep its liver after removing the bitter part, cut it into pieces and place everything in a saucepan with a piece of butter, a bouquet of parsley, chives, a clove of garlic, three cloves, two shallots, a bay leaf, thyme, and basil.
Pass it over the fire and add a full tablespoon of flour, moisten with half a septier of white wine, two spoonfuls of vinegar, two or three glasses of water or bouillon.
Cook for one hour, then have turnips cut neatly, blanch them for half a quarter hour in boiling water and put them to cook with the hare.
Season with salt and coarse pepper, finish cooking and serve at short sauce.
Remove the bouquet and serve hot. If the hare is tender, the turnips should be added at the same time.

title: Lièvre à la Broche (Roasted Hare on the Spit)
description: Prepared with hare, shallots, and bay leaf.
steps: When your hare is skinned and gutted, sear it on a hot stove
The meat must be somewhat firm so the larding needle enters more easily
Remove from the stove and dip your hand in the hare's blood
Pass your hand over the back and thighs
Lard the hare from the neck to the end of the thighs
Leave a distance of one inch between the loins and the thighs
Roast on the spit for one hour to cook the young hare
For the sauce: pound the raw liver with the back of your knife
Pass it through with a small piece of butter, a little shallots, parsley branches, a little thyme and bay leaf
Put three-quarters of a tablespoon of flour that you have heated with your seasoning
Add a glass of white wine and two glasses of bouillon
Stir your sauce until it boils
Add salt and pepper, enough so that pepper dominates
Reduce your sauce to more than half
When reduced, pass it through a sieve while pressing lightly
Serve your sauce in a sauce boat beside your roasted hare dish
Alternatively, you can roast a young hare on the spit without larding it; instead bard it from the neck to the thighs

title: Lièvre à la Saint-Denis (Hare Saint-Denis Style)
description: Prepared with hare, chives, and onions.

ingredients.name: Medium lardons, well seasoned with crushed aromatics, salt and pepper
ingredients.sourceText: Medium lardons, well seasoned with crushed aromatics, salt and pepper

ingredients.name: Lard fat, the same amount as the liver, finely chopped
ingredients.sourceText: Lard fat, the same amount as the liver, finely chopped

ingredients.name: Forcemeat for quenelles, twice the amount of the liver forcemeat
ingredients.sourceText: Forcemeat for quenelles, twice the amount of the liver forcemeat

ingredients.name: One bottle of good white wine
ingredients.sourceText: One bottle of good white wine

steps: When you have plucked your hare, clean it and make the smallest possible hole in its belly.
Cut off its head.
Season medium lardons to lard the fillets and thighs.
Place it to marinate for two or three days with salt, fine pepper, parsley sprigs, thyme, laurel, whole chives, and two sliced onions.
When you wish to serve it, finely chop the liver and chop an equal amount of fat lard together.
Add a little salt, some crushed aromatics, and coarse pepper.
Mix this forcemeat with twice as much quenelle forcemeat and blend them together.
Add three egg yolks and mix thoroughly.
Place this forcemeat in the body of the hare.
Sew up the belly skin so the forcemeat does not escape.
Place lard strips in a braising pan and the hare on top.
Cover it with lard strips.
Arrange around it some veal slices, two sliced carrots, three onions, a bouquet of parsley and chives, thyme, laurel, two cloves, a bottle of good white wine, and a little salt.
Simmer your hare for two hours or more if it is tough.
At the moment of serving, drain it, glaze it, and reduce the braising liquid until almost glazed.
Add two spoonfuls of espagnole sauce.
Place your hare on a plate with the sauce underneath.
If it is too seasoned, add a piece of butter the size of an egg and lemon juice.
If you have no espagnole, make a light roux and moisten it with the braising liquid in which your hare cooked.
Your sauce should be quite thin so you can reduce it by more than half.
At the moment of serving, strain it through a sieve and check the salt seasoning.
You can wrap this hare in lard strips, buttered paper, and put it on a spit, serving a poivrade underneath.

Season it with salt and coarse pepper inside
Tie it up

description: Prepared with duck, broth, and red wine.
steps: Pluck the macreuse and gut it, brown it over coals like poultry you wish to put on the spit

Put it in a small pot with lean broth, a glass of red wine, salt, pepper, a bouquet of parsley, chives, one garlic clove, two cloves, and a little savory

title: Macédoine à la Béchamel (Vegetable Medley with Béchamel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with béchamel, carrots, and turnips.
steps: Prepare many small roots and vegetables in equal and uniform portions, as described for vegetable medleys in entrées: carrots, turnips, small onions, peas, asparagus, white beans, green beans, artichoke hearts, eggplants, cauliflower, cucumbers, small fava beans, and all sorts of roots and vegetables.
When the vegetables are cooked in appropriate seasoning, drain them until completely dry.
Put everything in a saucepan.
Make a somewhat reduced and bound béchamel sauce and pour it over your vegetable medley.
Toss to mix the sauce with the vegetables.
If you do not have béchamel, reduce velouté and add a liaison of three egg yolks.
Pass the velouté through a fine cloth.
Put on top an amount of butter the size of an egg.
If not using velouté, clarify the cooking liquid from your roots and make a white roux.
Moisten with the clarified cooking liquid.
Add a bay leaf and mushrooms.
Reduce your sauce so it is somewhat bound.
Add a liaison of three egg yolks and pass the sauce through a fine cloth over the vegetables, adding an amount of butter the size of an egg.
Toss the vegetables in the sauce so the vegetable medley is well coated.
Keep it hot without boiling.

description: Prepared with partridges, shallots, and bay leaf.
steps: Spit-roast 4 partridges and piece them as for partridge salmi

If you have no Spanish sauce, make a roux; add your pounded scraps, 1 glass of white wine, 2 glasses of bouillon, and 1 clove
Reduce the sauce, degrease it, and strain through fine cloth
Check the seasoning

description: A sauce made with mackerel, chives, and lemon juice.
steps: Empty the mackerel and remove the intestines by inserting the knife tip in the hole in the middle of the body

Split them from the back side from head to tail
Place them on an earthenware platter

Add half a glass of water and lemon juice
Place your sauce on the fire and stir constantly
At the first boil, if it tastes good, pour it over your mackerel

title: Marmelade d'Abricots sans Façon (Simple Apricot Jam)
description: A fruit preserve made with apricots and sugar.

ingredients.name: four and a half pounds of sugar
ingredients.sourceText: four and a half pounds of sugar

steps: Cut as thinly as you can six pounds of not-too-ripe apricots and put them as you go into a clean pot. Crack the pits, remove their skin and cut them very fine to add with the apricots. Pound four and a half pounds of sugar to put with the apricots. Put your pot on a clear fire and stir constantly with a skimming spoon for fear the jam sticks to the bottom. When the apricots are well advanced in cooking, remove the pot from time to time to crush the pieces of apricots that do not turn to jam. Cook until it sticks to your fingers without much resistance, testing by taking some jam in your fingers and pressing them together. Then put it in pots. This method, though simple, is very good.

When the apricots are well advanced in cooking, remove the pot from time to time to crush the pieces of apricots that do not turn to jam. Cook until it sticks to your fingers without much resistance, testing by taking some jam in your fingers and pressing them together. Then put it in pots. This method, though simple, is very good.

title: Marmelade de Fleurs d'Orange (Orange Blossom Jam)
description: A fruit preserve made with orange, juice, and sugar.

ingredients.name: half a pound of orange blossoms
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of orange blossoms

steps: Put five quarterons of sugar in a pan with half a setier of water. Bring to a boil and skim well. Continue boiling until dipping the skimming spoon in and shaking it over the sugar, blowing through the holes produces little sparks of sugar. Then add your orange blossom prepared as follows: take half a pound of peeled orange blossoms and boil for half a quarter hour in water. Remove this water from the fire and add a small pinch of alum. Put fresh water on the fire. When it boils, add the juice of one lemon, put your orange blossom in it, and remove with the skimming spoon letting it drain. Boil it in the lemon water until it is tender under the fingers. Then put it for half an hour in fresh water with a little lemon juice. Then press the orange blossom in a cloth to remove the water, and pound in a mortar to make jam. Put this jam in the sugar to blend them together, pouring the sugar several times over a very small fire, without letting it boil or even simmer. Put in pots and sprinkle a little fine sugar on top when cold.

title: Marrons à l'Espagnole (Chestnuts Spanish Style)
description: Prepared with chestnuts, espagnole, and consommé.

ingredients.name: half a quarter pound of butter
ingredients.sourceText: half a quarter pound of butter

steps: Take fifty chestnuts (they should not be from Lyon, as they are not good for cooking).
Blanch them in hot water like almonds.
Take great care to remove all the second skin so they have no bitterness.
When well blanched, put them in a saucepan with half a quarter pound of butter, four spoonfuls of espagnole sauce, two glasses of consommé, a bay leaf, and a little grated nutmeg.
Boil the chestnuts for half an hour.
Then remove them from their sauce and put them in another saucepan.
Let the sauce reduce and pass it through a fine cloth over the chestnuts.
Keep them hot in a bain-marie.
At the moment of serving, arrange them on the dish with the sauce underneath.
You can also serve them with various sauces.

description: Prepared with sweet almonds, egg whites, and apricot or marmalade or liquid or preserves.

ingredients.name: sweet almonds, blanched and peeled

ingredients.name: Apricot marmalade or other non-liquid preserves

steps: Take one pound of sweet almonds that you have blanched and peeled, pound them
While pounding, sprinkle them with three egg whites
Mix them then with apricot marmalade or other non-liquid preserves, candied and pounded orange flowers
When all is well mixed, place your almonds in a saucepan with sugar powder and dry them over the fire
Place them then on a table and work them with fine sugar
Add sugar until the paste no longer sticks to your hands
Roll it then to form marzipans of whatever shape you wish
Take six egg whites that you whip half-way and mix with chopped green citron
Dip the marzipans in this mixture and place them after in fine sugar as much as they can take
Arrange them on sheets of white paper, which you place on copper sheets, and bake them in the oven with gentle heat
To be sure of the oven temperature, put a little paste on a card; if the card takes on color, it is a sign that the oven is too hot

description: Prepared with fish, white wine, and onions.

At the moment of serving, arrange on a plat with bread crusts sautéed in butter around it
Garnish the stew with crayfish

description: Prepared with larks, shallots, and mushrooms.
steps: Pluck, truss and singe your larks; place a good piece of butter in a casserole with fifteen or eighteen larks, salt, coarse pepper, and a little pounded aromatic herbs; place them on a hot fire

Once you have sautéed them in your butter for seven or eight minutes, add about one spoonful of finely chopped parsley, the same amount of finely chopped shallots, and chopped mushrooms; sauté them with fine herbs for seven or eight minutes
Pour in about two skimming-spoonfuls of espagnole and one spoonful of bouillon; stir them in their sauce over the fire; at the first boil, remove them and serve them

If you do not have sauce, add one spoonful of flour, mix it well with your birds; add half a glass of white wine and as much bouillon; bring your sauce to a single boil; check that your ragout is properly seasoned

title: Mauviettes en Croustades (Larks in Pastry Cases)
description: Deboned larks are filled with seasoned forcemeat and served inside hollowed, butter-browned bread cases. The filled cases are heated in the oven and finished with Italienne sauce.
steps: Debone twelve larks; take the interior, except the gizzard; chop it and mix this hash with an equal amount of cooked forcemeat, a little grated nutmeg, a little salt and coarse pepper, and a little fine herbs
Place this forcemeat on a silver platter, with a strip of lard on top; place it on a gentle stove with a camp oven over it; once your forcemeat is cooked, put it in a casserole

Pour in about two skimming-spoonfuls of velouté and mix well with your forcemeat; fill the interior of your larks with this; give them the shape of a small ball or an oval if you wish; sew them with thread so they do not lose their shape
Place a piece of butter in a casserole; warm it gently; add your larks with a little salt, coarse pepper, and a little quatre épices; place them on a gentle fire for seven or eight minutes

Once well stiffened, drain them; prepare croutons made with thick-cut bread about an inch and a half thick; make an incision inside at a line from the edge; pass them through butter; when they have a nice color, remove them from the butter and drain them on white linen; hollow out the bread; put some of your forcemeat inside, and your lark from which you have removed the thread; leave a little space above your forcemeat to add some sauce

Fifteen minutes before serving, place your croutons garnished with larks on a tourtière and put them in the oven or under a not-too-hot camp oven; at the moment of serving, arrange your croutons on the plate and put a little italienne sauce in each one

title: Morue en Dauphin (Fresh Cod Shaped as a Dolphin)
description: Prepared with cod, chives, and garlic.
steps: Season the cod with salt, pepper, parsley, chives, garlic, and bay leaf
Take an iron skewer called a hatelet and pass it through the fresh cod starting at the eyes, through the middle of the body, and finishing at the tail, shaping it to look like a dolphin
Place it on a baking dish and baste it with its marinade
Cook it in the oven
When cooked, remove the skewer and arrange it on the serving platter
For the ragout: boil three carp roe briefly in water; also boil asparagus tips briefly in water
Put everything in a saucepan with a good piece of butter, mushrooms, and a bouquet of parsley and chives
Pass over the fire and add a pinch of flour, then moisten with a glass of white wine and good lean broth
When the ragout is cooked and the sauce is reduced and seasoned to taste, add a liaison of three egg yolks and cream
Bind the sauce over the fire and serve over the cod
For best results, add the asparagus only when the ragout is nearly finished

title: Noix de Veau en Ballotine (Veal Cushion Ballottine)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and shallots.

ingredients.name: One veal cushion, with or without teat
ingredients.sourceText: One veal cushion, with or without teat

steps: Lard the veal cushion with thick lard in the same manner as veal in the bourgeoise style, with the same seasoning in the larding pieces
Place half a pound of butter in a casserole and put the cushion in it
Sauté over fire for three-quarters of an hour without allowing it to take color
Dust with salt and coarse pepper
Remove from the casserole and place on a plate
If there is juice in the casserole with the butter, reduce it until the butter becomes oil
Add the grated lard and oil
Add finely chopped shallots (one spoonful) and let them fry a little in the butter
Add a dozen finely chopped mushrooms, pass them with the butter, and add parsley (one spoonful)
When all is well combined, add grated nutmeg and coarse pepper
Pour the fine herbs over the veal cushion
When cooled, oil six sheets of paper
Wrap the cushion with a thin lard bard on top and bottom, then wrap it with a sheet of paper so the seasoning does not escape, then cover with another sheet, continuing until all six sheets are used
Ensure the cushion is hermetically sealed, the bundle has a fine shape, and the folds are well made
Tie the bundle with string as one ties a piece of beef, so the paper does not come undone on the grill
One hour before serving, place the cushion on the grill with very gentle heat
Watch that the paper does not burn and the seasoning does not escape
When the cushion is grilled, remove only the string and serve the cushion in the paper with the sauce inside
If the first sheet is too dark, it should be removed

title: Noix de Veau en Surprise (Veal Cushion en Surprise)
description: Prepared with veal, fat, and lard.

ingredients.name: Four onions, one studded with two cloves
ingredients.sourceText: Four onions, one studded with two cloves

ingredients.name: A bouquet of parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: A bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: Prepare the cushion as for veal à la Conty: lard it with thick and thin larding fat
Place lard bards in the bottom of a casserole or braising pan
Add veal slices, two carrots, four onions (one studded with two cloves), one bay leaf, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and a little salt
Place the veal cushion in the casserole
Cover only the teat with lard bards
Butter a round double sheet of paper and cook the cushion with fire on top and below
When the cushion is cooked, let it cool
Make an oval hole and remove the flesh, leaving enough at the bottom so the cushion can hold a ragout without leaking
Cut the meat removed from the cushion into small dice, except for the top, which you preserve to mask the ragout so one cannot see the cushion has been opened
Also cut mushrooms into small dice and add them with the meat to a béchamel sauce
Heat the veal cushion
At serving time, drain it well and glaze it
Pour the small ragout into the hollow of the cushion
Cover it with the top you have preserved so one cannot see the cushion has been opened
It must be glazed, and you will put Spanish sauce underneath

title: Noix de Veau Piquée Glacée (Larded and Glazed Veal Cushion)
description: Prepared with veal, fat, and lard.

ingredients.name: Four onions, one studded with two cloves
ingredients.sourceText: Four onions, one studded with two cloves

ingredients.name: A bouquet of parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: A bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: Beat the veal cushion well
Remove the skin and teat covering the cushion
Place the meat skin-side down on the table
With a sharp knife, slip it between the top nervous layer and the flesh, as if lifting a bard, being careful not to cut too deeply into the meat to minimize waste and keep the cushion well-formed
Remove any remaining skin as gently as possible so no knife marks are visible
Lard the prepared cushion with thin larding fat
Place lard bards in a casserole with a few veal slices, two or three carrots, four onions (one studded with two cloves), one bay leaf, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Position the cushion in the casserole so it rounds in the middle
Cover with a double sheet of buttered paper
Add one spoonful of consommé
Bring to a boil; when it has thrown off a few bubbles, place on gentle heat and put fire on the lid
Cook for two hours
At serving time, drain it well, glaze it, and serve underneath with chicory, cream, cucumbers, and either glazing sauce or tomato sauce as you see fit

title: Noix de Veau Piquée à la Conty (Veal Knuckle Larded in the Conty Style)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and carrots.

ingredients.name: One veal knuckle, whole and well covered
ingredients.sourceText: One veal knuckle, whole and well covered

ingredients.name: Three carrots, turned into large batons
ingredients.sourceText: Three carrots, turned into large batons

ingredients.name: One spoonful of jelly or consommé or bouillon
ingredients.sourceText: One spoonful of jelly or consommé or bouillon

steps: Remove your knuckle whole and well covered
Beat it like the previous one
Pare the flesh that is under the nipple, without touching the nipple
Lard with fine lard the flesh that appears from your knuckle
When your knuckle is larded with fine lard, lard it underneath with coarse lard
Season the lardoons with salt and coarse pepper
When your knuckle is larded, truss it like the previous one
Put it in a casserole
Cover it with buttered paper

Put in three carrots turned into large batons, four large onions, one of which is studded with two cloves, two laurel leaves, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and one spoonful of jelly; if you have no jelly, put consommé or bouillon in it
Cook your knuckle on a gentle fire for two hours, fire above, fire below

When your knuckle is three-quarters cooked, remove your vegetables with your knuckle, and make it fall to glaze, that is to say put it on a hot fire, and reduce the liquid of your knuckle until it is glazed
At the moment of serving, remove your knuckle from your casserole
Untie it
Glaze it with what is in your casserole
Put three spoonfuls of grande Espagnole sauce in your casserole, where you will have removed the fat, and loosened the glaze
Put this sauce under your knuckle; in case you have no sauce, you would put a little flour in it that you would loosen with a little bouillon

title: Noix de Veau à la Bourgeoise (Veal Knuckle with Vegetables)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Four large carrots, turned into large batons
ingredients.sourceText: Four large carrots, turned into large batons

steps: Remove your knuckle of veal well trimmed
Place it in a white cloth
Beat it with a cleaver
Lard it with large lard
Season your lardoons with fine salt, pepper, four spices, parsley and very finely minced chive, a little thyme and laurel also minced, which you mix well with your lardoons
Your knuckle must be well larded
Keep your knuckle covered with its skins, taking care that the lardoons do not pierce the skin on top
Tie it with a trussing needle and string that you put around, so that the skins covering your knuckle do not curl back, and when cooked they are well covered
Butter the bottom of your casserole
Put your veal knuckle in it
Also put around four carrots which you turn into large batons, four large onions, two laurel leaves, two full glasses of bouillon
Cover your knuckle with a round of buttered paper
When your knuckle boils, put it on a gentle fire for two hours
Put a little fire on the cover of your casserole
At the moment of serving, drain your veal knuckle
Untie it
Put underneath the stock which you reduce by half, and the vegetables that cooked with your knuckle
Glaze it if you have glaze; you can serve with this knuckle, while glazing it, a glaze sauce, a tomato sauce, chicory, an oseille purée, lettuces, a mushroom purée, etc.

title: Oeufs au Gratin (Eggs au Gratin)
description: Prepared with eggs, bread crumbs, and anchovy.
steps: Take a heat-safe dish and place on it a small gratin made with bread crumbs, a good piece of butter, chopped anchovy, parsley, chives, and shallot, all chopped together
Mix in three egg yolks and combine everything
Place this mixture in the bottom of the dish to the thickness of a coin and let it set on a low fire
Then break seven or eight eggs on top and season with salt and coarse pepper
Cook gently and pass a red-hot iron or shovel over the top
When cooked with soft yolks, serve

title: Oeufs Brouillés à la Coque (Scrambled Eggs in the Shell)
description: Prepared with eggs, bread crumbs, and chives.
steps: Cut as many rounds of bread crumbs as you wish to serve eggs, shaped like a small snuff box
Make a small hole in the middle to hold an egg lengthwise
Take the eggs you wish to scramble and break them quickly at one end to empty them
Scramble them by putting them in a saucepan with a small piece of butter, a little chopped parsley and chives, salt, coarse pepper, and two spoonfuls of cream
Cook on the fire while stirring constantly until they are cooked
Return them to their cleaned and drained shells and place them on the bread crumb bases

title: Oeufs en Croquettes (Egg Croquettes)
description: Prepared with egg, cream, and bread.

ingredients.name: parsley and chives, finely chopped and washed
ingredients.sourceText: parsley and chives, finely chopped and washed

steps: Hard boil eighteen eggs
Cut the whites and yolks into small dice
Put them in a saucepan
Make a cream sauce in which you put a little finely chopped and washed parsley and chives
Pour it over your eggs; they should be somewhat bound together
Stir them in their sauce
Let the mixture cool
Take a spoonful and pour it onto a board
When the eggs are well cold, shape them into croquettes
Roll them in bread crumb
Dip in beaten egg and bread them a second time
At the moment of service, put them in very hot oil
When they have a nice color, drain them on white cloth or in a strainer
Arrange them on the dish

description: Prepared with eggs, chives, and mushrooms.
steps: Put in a saucepan a piece of butter with parsley, chives, mushrooms, and shallots, all chopped

Bread it with bread crumbs and pour butter over it again
Brown it underneath a pie-dish lid

description: Prepared with eggs, butter, and salt.
steps: Melt a little butter to coat the inside of six copper goblets or small timbales

Serve with clear jus

title: Oeufs Farcis (Stuffed Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, bread, and chives.

ingredients.name: an equal portion of butter and egg yolks
ingredients.sourceText: an equal portion of butter and egg yolks

ingredients.name: chives and parsley, finely chopped and washed
ingredients.sourceText: chives and parsley, finely chopped and washed

steps: Hard boil ten eggs
Cut them in half lengthwise
Remove the yolks and pound them in a mortar
Pass them through a quenelle sieve
Soak a bread crumb in milk and press well to extract the milk; pound it and pass it through a sieve along with the eggs
Pound as much butter in the mortar as you have pounded yolks
Mix equal portions of butter and egg yolks together
When your stuffing is well pounded, add a little finely chopped and washed chives and parsley, salt, coarse pepper, and a little grated nutmeg
Pound the stuffing again
Add two or three whole egg yolks; keep the stuffing workable by adding egg as needed
When finished, place it in a vessel
Arrange it a finger's thickness in the bottom of the dish
Stuff your egg halves
Dip a knife blade in egg white to smooth the top
Arrange the eggs in order on the stuffing in the dish
Place it on red coals with a field oven on top
When they have a nice color, serve them

description: Prepared with vinegar, water, and salt.

description: Prepared with eggs, powdered sugar, and orange.

ingredients.name: a little orange flower powder or other flavoring
ingredients.sourceText: a little orange flower powder or other flavoring

steps: Break ten eggs and separate the whites and yolks
Beat the whites as you would for a biscuit; when they are well set, add two spoonfuls of powdered sugar and a little orange flower powder
Pour a pint of milk into a saucepan with six ounces of sugar and a little orange flower powder or other flavoring
When the milk boils, take a spoonful of the beaten whites and put it in the milk; poach the whites
Let them drain on a sieve; when all are poached, remove half the milk or only a quarter of it
Blend the yolks and put them in the milk; stir with a wooden spoon
When you see them binding together, remove from heat and strain through cheesecloth into another saucepan
Arrange the eggs on the dish and mask them with your sauce

Roast on a spit

title: Oie à la Moutarde (Goose with Mustard)
description: Prepared with goose, mustard, and goose liver.
steps: Singe, pluck, and eviscerate a young tender goose

Chop the liver after removing the bitter part and mix it with two chopped shallots, parsley, chives, a laurel leaf, thyme and basil (chopped like powder), a good piece of butter, salt, and coarse pepper
Stuff the goose and sew it closed
Roast it on a spit, basting from time to time with a little butter
As you baste, hold a plate underneath to catch what falls
When the goose is almost cooked, mix one spoonful of mustard into the butter used for basting
Spread it back on the goose and bread it gradually until the entire top is well covered with breadcrumbs
Finish cooking until it has a beautiful golden color

For the sauce: in a casserole, place butter the size of half an egg mixed with two pinches of flour, one good spoonful of mustard, one teaspoonful of vinegar, and a small glass of bouillon, salt, and coarse pepper; bind over the fire
Serve the sauce under the goose

title: Omelette aux Truffes (Truffle Omelet)
description: Prepared with truffles, espagnole, and bouillon.
steps: Break eggs, season and beat them.
Put a piece of butter in a pan over a clear fire.
As soon as it is melted, add the eggs.
Stir the omelet by shaking so it does not stick, or with a fork or spoon, lift them until your omelet is set.
Remove the bulk of the inside with a spoon.
Take truffles sautéed in a reduced espagnole sauce and put them in the void you have made in the omelet.
Fold it so it has the shape of a turnover.
Place it on the dish.
Chop two truffes very finely.
Pass them in a small piece of butter.
Add four spoonfuls of espagnole sauce and pour your sauce hot over the omelet.

If you do not want to use sauce, take a teaspoonful of flour that you mix with your truffles when they are cooked, and moisten them with bouillon, jus, a little salt, coarse pepper, and very little quatre épices.
By this same procedure, you can make omelets with mushrooms, with poultry or game purée, etc.

title: Omelette Soufflée (Soufflé Omelet)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, lemon, and eggs.
steps: Break six eggs and separate the whites and yolks.
Add four spoonfuls of powdered sugar.
Chop very finely half the zest of a lemon skin and put it with the yolks.
Mix them with the sugar and lemon.
At the moment of serving the dish, whip your egg whites as for a biscuit.
Mix the yolks well with the whites.
Then put a quarter pound of butter in the pan over a fire not too hot.
As soon as the butter is melted, add the eggs.
Stir the omelet so the bottom comes to the top.
When you see that the omelet has absorbed the butter, pour it as a turnover onto a buttered dish and place it on a bed of red coals.
Throw powdered sugar over the omelet.
Place a very hot camp oven over it.
Take care lest your omelet take too much color.

description: Prepared with pig's ears, onions, and vinegar.
steps: Cook the pig's ears in the same seasoning as for hure (head cheese).
When they are cold, cut them into small strips and place them in a casserole.
Cut twelve large onions in half, remove the head and tail, and cut them in semi-circles.
Pass the onions in a good piece of butter until they are well browned.
If you do not have sauce, add one tablespoon of flour which you stir with your onions.
Add half a glass of vinegar, one glass of bouillon, salt, and coarse pepper.
Let the onions come to a boil a few times.
Place them over your sliced pig's ears.
Sauté everything together and keep it warm without boiling.
At the moment of serving, arrange your ragout on the plate and surround it with croutons.

Put your lentils in a cloth strainer, remove the bouillon, and press them through with a wooden spoon.

description: Prepared with cheese, white wine, and broth.

ingredients.name: a bouquet of parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: a bouquet of parsley and chives

ingredients.name: a handful of crumb of bread
ingredients.sourceText: a handful of crumb of bread

ingredients.name: a bit of grated Gruyère cheese

ingredients.name: a mixture of bread crumb and grated Gruyère cheese
ingredients.sourceText: a mixture of bread crumb and grated Gruyère cheese

steps: Scald six calf's ears well
Blanch them for a quarter hour in boiling water
Remove to cold water and clean off any remaining hairs
Put them to cook with a glass of white wine and twice as much broth, salt, pepper, a bouquet of parsley and chives, a clove of garlic, two cloves, a half bay leaf, thyme, basil, and a little butter
When cooked, drain them
Make a stuffing: heat a handful of bread crumb over the fire with a half-setier of milk and a bit of grated Gruyère cheese
Stir until the bread crumb is well thickened
Let cool, then add a little butter and four raw egg yolks
Mix together and stuff the inside of the ears
Dip the ears in warm butter to bread them, using a mixture of half bread crumb and half grated Gruyère cheese
Arrange in the serving dish
Brown them nicely under a pastry cover
Wipe the edges of the dish and serve without sauce

title: Oysters in Hash (Huîtres en Hachis)
description: Prepared with oysters, chives, and mushrooms.
steps: Take fifty oysters in a basket that you put in hot water; when it is ready to boil, you remove it to put them in fresh water, drain them, and then take only the tender parts.
If you take all of it, let the hard part be chopped very fine.
Put the rest with it to chop as well.
If you wish to mix with carp meat, that will increase your hash and give it good taste.

Put in a pot a good piece of butter, with parsley, chive, chopped mushrooms, pass them over the fire and add a pinch of flour; moisten them afterwards with half a setier of white wine and as much lean bouillon.
Put in to cook your hash, until there is no more sauce, and season it to good taste.
When you are ready to serve, add a liaison of three egg yolks and cream; serve for an entrée.

description: Prepared with partridges, lard, and salt pork.
steps: Prepare partridges as for stewed partridges
Place bards of lard in a casserole with the partridges, a pound of blanched and cleaned salt pork, a large cervelat or a piece of ham, and a few slices of veal

Add four carrots, four onions, two cloves, and two bay leaves
Blanch the cabbage, tie with twine, and press them
Place the cabbage on top of the partridges

Add two spoonfuls of bouillon
Simmer for two hours
At service, drain and untie them
Dress on a platter
Drain and press the cabbage to dry, and dress around the partridges
Cut the lard into pieces and place at intervals on the cabbage with the cervelat
Top with espagnole sauce

description: Prepared with partridges, juice, and lard.

ingredients.name: Three fresh partridges of the same size
ingredients.sourceText: Three fresh partridges of the same size

ingredients.name: Three-quarters of a pound of butter
ingredients.sourceText: Three-quarters of a pound of butter

steps: Select three fresh partridges of equal size, not skinned on the breast or bruised
Empty them through the vent, removing the intestines, gizzard, and liver to avoid making incisions elsewhere
Singe them lightly when well plucked
Mix three-quarters of a pound of butter with a little salt, the juice of one lemon, some coarse pepper, and pounded aromatic herbs, all well combined
Fill your partridges with this butter
Truss and tie them as you would a braised hen
Place strips of lard in a casserole, put the partridges on top
Cover them with lemon slices and strips of lard
Pour a poêle over them
Simmer for a good half hour
Drain them
At the moment of serving, remove the trussing strings and arrange on the platter
Place a fine crayfish between each partridge
Add three spoonfuls of Spanish sauce and three spoonfuls of game essence reduced by half, and pour under the partridges
If you do not have sauce or game essence, make a light roux and strain through silk sieve the cooking liquid from the partridges
Moisten it and add half a glass of white wine
If your sauce is too thin, reduce it until it is thick enough to sauce the partridges
Be sure to skim it and strain it through a fine sieve
Check that it is properly salted

steps: Place partridges on a moderately hot fire

When well browned, add six spoonfuls of Spanish sauce, half a bottle of white wine, a bay leaf, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and a clove
Simmer the partridges for three quarters of an hour
Remove them when cooked and place in a casserole
Skim the sauce and reduce it by half
Strain it through a sieve over the partridges
At the moment of serving, remove the trussing strings and arrange on the platter
Serve the sauce underneath

If you do not have Spanish sauce, leave the partridges in their butter, make a light roux which you will moisten with white wine and half a bottle of bouillon, pour this over the partridges with the seasoning
When you reduce your sauce, skim it as much as possible and reduce it until it is thick enough to serve as sauce
Check that it is properly salted

steps: Empty and singe your partridges
Truss them as you would a braised hen
Put them on the spit
When cooked, let them cool
Remove the breast meat in such a way that the rest of the body forms an oval well
Cut the meat into small dice and put in a casserole
Cut two or three truffles also into small dice
Have about twenty mushrooms, cut them small
Mix them together with your truffles and your partridge meat
Add six spoonfuls of Spanish sauce and six spoonfuls of game essence
Reduce everything by a third
Strain through a fine sieve over your small ragout
Keep your partridges warm in a casserole
At the moment of serving, remove the trussing strings
Put your ragout inside your partridges with Spanish sauce underneath

title: Perdreaux à la Saint-Laurent (Partridges Saint-Laurent)
description: Prepared with partridges, sauce, and juice.

ingredients.name: or: fine bread crumbs (brown crusts), 7 or 8 shallots, pepper, salt, 1/2 glass of water, 6 tablespoons of vinegar, 4 tablespoons of oil
ingredients.sourceText: or: fine bread crumbs (brown crusts), 7 or 8 shallots, pepper, salt, 1/2 glass of water, 6 tablespoons of vinegar, 4 tablespoons of oil

steps: Clean and singe your partridges; cut off the legs and truss the thighs inside without making a large hole near the croupion
Split the partridge down the back from neck to croupion
Spread open the partridge and flatten it on the breast so it has a greater surface area
Dust with salt and coarse pepper
Place the breast side in a saucepan with oil and brown it over heat
Turn to the other side to brown equally
Half an hour before serving, place on a grill over moderate heat
Take {{source-4}}, juice of 1.5 lemons, and zest it slightly to put in your sauce with salt and coarse pepper; bring the sauce to a boil once only
Place the partridge on the platter and sauce over it
If you have neither sauce nor lemon, finely bread some brown bread crusts; chop 7 or 8 shallots with a little pepper and salt, 1/2 glass of water, 6 tablespoons of vinegar, and 4 tablespoons of oil
Bring this sauce to a boil 2 or 3 times and place it over your partridge

title: Petit Salé de Cochon (Cured Pork)
description: Prepared with pork and salt.
steps: Cut pork into pieces of desired size
Crush salt; for every 15 pounds of meat, use 1 pound of salt
Rub the meat thoroughly with salt
Place in a vessel as it is salted
When full, seal the vessel well to prevent air exposure
Can be used after 5 or 6 days
For longer storage, use slightly more salt
Note that fresher cured meat is better
Serve with pea purée, cabbage ragout, vegetable ragout, lentil purée, or turnip purée
Do not add salt to the accompanying ragout

title: Petite Bécassine (Small Snipe)
description: Prepared with shallots, juice, and white wine.

ingredients.name: Half a glass of white wine
ingredients.sourceText: Half a glass of white wine

steps: Truss your snipes, singe them and pluck them
Put a good piece of butter in a casserole with your snipes, chopped shallots, a little grated nutmeg, salt, and coarse pepper
Cook them on a hot fire; when you have sautéed them for seven or eight minutes, add the juice of two lemons, half a glass of white wine, and a little bread crumbs
Leave them on the fire until your sauce has come to a boil; then remove them from the fire and serve

title: Petite Béchamel (Small Béchamel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with veal, ham, and carrots.

ingredients.name: approximately one pound veal cut into dice
ingredients.sourceText: approximately one pound veal cut into dice

ingredients.name: one half-pound ham cut into dice
ingredients.sourceText: one half-pound ham cut into dice

steps: Place the veal, ham, carrots, onions, cloves, bay leaves, basil, and butter in a saucepan
Brown the mixture over heat, stirring with a spoon and being careful that the meat does not take on color
When the meat is well browned, add the wheat flour and stir
When the flour is well mixed with the butter and meat, add the milk
Stir constantly so the sauce does not stick
Simmer over moderate heat for one hour and a half
If the sauce reduces too much, add more milk or broth
The sauce should have the consistency of porridge when served
If it is too thick, add a little milk, cream, or broth
Do not oversalt this sauce because of the ham and because it must be reduced
Strain through a sieve
