title: Petits Pois Verts au Petit Beurre (Green Peas with Butter)
description: Prepared with peas, butter, and chives.
steps: Take two liters of peas.
Put a quarter pound of butter in them.
Sprinkle with water and knead them together with your hands.
Let them drain in a strainer.
Put them in a saucepan over a hot fire.
Sauté the peas when they have felt the heat well.
Moisten them with boiling water.
Add salt, black pepper, the equivalent of half a walnut of sugar, a bouquet of parsley and chives.
Reduce the liquid until there is almost none left.
At the moment of serving, when the peas are boiling, add three small pieces of butter, or about the size of two eggs of butter.
Sauté them without putting them on the fire until they are well bound.
Arrange them in a bush shape; check that they have good salt.

title: Petits Pois à la Bourgeoise (Peas Bourgeoise)
description: Prepared with peas, onions, and chives.
steps: Make a light white roux.
Add the peas; when they are well browned, moisten with boiling water.
Add salt, pepper, four onions, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and sliced romaine lettuce.
Let them reduce while cooking.
When the peas are cooked and at the moment of serving, add a liaison of three egg yolks.
Do not let them boil with the liaison for fear it will break; make sure they are well seasoned.

title: Petits Pots à la Fleur d'Orange (Small Pots with Orange Flower Water)
description: Prepared with cream or milk, candied orange, and sugar.

ingredients.name: Seven measures of cream or good milk
ingredients.sourceText: Seven measures of cream or good milk

ingredients.name: One spoonful of candied orange flower water
ingredients.sourceText: One spoonful of candied orange flower water

steps: Measure seven times one small pot of cream or good milk and put in {{source-1}} and one spoonful of candied orange flower water
Bring your milk to a boil and let it cool
If your pots are large, put seven egg yolks; if small, five are sufficient
Mix them with your milk and strain the composition four or five times through cloth
Check that the cream tastes good and pour it into your small pots
Put water in a large saucepan and bring it to boil and place the small pots in it
They must be placed in the boiling water only up to three-quarters height so water does not enter; place the lid of the saucepan and put fire on top
Let your water bath go very gently
After ten minutes, check if your small pots are set; remove them, dry them, and serve them cold
You can give these small pots any flavor you wish: orange flower, lemon, tea, vanilla, violet, etc.

title: Petits-Pâtés Friands (Small Savory Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with veal, beef marrow, and cream.

ingredients.name: beef marrow equal in amount to the veal
ingredients.sourceText: beef marrow equal in amount to the veal

ingredients.name: parsley, chives, and mushrooms, all chopped
ingredients.sourceText: parsley, chives, and mushrooms, all chopped

ingredients.name: cooked chicken breast from the spit
ingredients.sourceText: cooked chicken breast from the spit

steps: Make small ordinary pastries with puff pastry
Chop together a piece of veal round and beef marrow
Add chopped parsley, chives, and mushrooms
Mix in two whole eggs, salt, and pepper
Dilute this mixture with half a setier of cream and taste to correct seasoning
Use small pastry molds and line with thin layers of puff pastry about the thickness of a small coin
Spread some of this forcemeat on the pastry and cover with another layer of pastry
Glaze with egg and bake in the oven
While they bake, chop cooked chicken breast very finely
Put about one chopine of good bouillon in a saucepan with a small bouquet of mixed herbs and a little butter
Reduce the bouillon to a quarter of its volume and remove the bouquet
Add the chopped chicken breast and a little salt
Heat without boiling and add a liaison of three egg yolks mixed with cream
Thicken on the fire and add lemon juice
When the pastries are removed from the oven, remove the top of each to take out the meat
Replace the meat with a spoonful of the chicken ragout
Replace the cover on each small pastry and serve as hot as possible

title: Pheasant Périgord Style (Faisan à la Périgordux)
description: Prepared with pheasant, truffles, and lard.

ingredients.name: One and a half pounds of truffles
ingredients.sourceText: One and a half pounds of truffles

steps: Empty and singe your pheasant; break the two breast bones; it must be emptied by the pocket so as not to damage the croup of your pheasant
Have a pound and a half of truffles which you clean and peel, that is to say remove the top layer of your truffles which you set aside
Chop them very finely; place then a half pound of grated lard in a casserole, a quarter pound of butter, a quarter pound of oil which you will heat
Put your truffles cut into pieces about the size of a large nut; sauté them; add a little salt, a little coarse pepper, a little of the four spices
When the truffles have boiled in your lard for five minutes, put your chopped trimmed pieces in; let them cool, and put everything by the pocket in the body of the pheasant
Arrange a very thin slice of lard bacon on the place where your truffles entered, and put the skin back on top
Truss the legs as for a roasted hen; bind them well; fasten the skin of the pocket so the truffles do not come out while cooking
Put lard bacon in a casserole, your pheasant on top; cover it well with bacon; mark a braising pan without lemon which you will put on top; cover it

title: Pheasant with Truffles (Faisan aux Truffes)
description: Prepared with truffles, lard, and pheasant.
steps: Boil the truffles in lard for five minutes
Add finely chopped pheasant trimmings and let cool
Using a piping bag, fill the pheasant body with the mixture
Arrange a thin bard of lard over the opening where the truffles were inserted and cover with skin
Truss the legs as for a braised hen and tie securely
Secure the pocket skin so truffles do not escape during cooking
Place bards of lard in a casserole with the pheasant on top
Cover well with bards and place a braising pan (poêle) without lemon on top
Cover with a round of buttered paper and simmer for one hour
At service, drain the pheasant and untie carefully without tearing
Dress on a platter
Chop two truffles and pass through butter

description: Prepared with lamb, cooking liquid, and velouté.

Put them to disgorge
Blanch them
Refresh them
Drain them
Dry them
Singe them
Remove the hair found in the cleft of the foot
Put them to cook in a blanc
Let them simmer for two hours
Feel them; if they are not cooked enough, then boil them for another half hour
Drain them
Trim them
Put them in a saucepan
Pour in four spoonfuls of worked velouté
Add some finely chopped parsley
Add to your sauce a liaison of one egg
When your sauce is bound, pour it over your lamb feet, stirring them well in your sauce
At the moment of serving, add lemon juice, a little coarse pepper, and dress your feet on your platter
Check that they are properly seasoned

title: Pieds de Cochon Farcis aux Truffes (Pig's Feet Stuffed with Truffles)
description: Prepared with pig's feet, truffles, and bay leaf.
steps: Prepare your half pig's feet and cook them in the same seasoning as those prepared à la Sainte-Menehould.
Simmer them for eight hours.
Remove them from their cooking liquid when they are half cold.
Unwrap your feet and remove the bones.

Make a forcemeat with cooked chicken breasts; chop and pound bread crumbs; dry in bouillon over the fire the veal udder, using as much bread as chicken, as much udder as bread and chicken combined, all well pounded.
Mix in three or four egg yolks, chopped truffles, a little four spices, salt, coarse pepper, and a little cream.
When your forcemeat is finished, add truffles cut in slices.
Fill the interior of the foot in place of the bones with your forcemeat.
Cover this forcemeat with pork or veal caul.
Take care to preserve the shape of your feet.
Dip them in warm butter and coat them with breadcrumbs.
Fifteen minutes and a half before serving, place them on a grill over a gentle fire.
Pay attention that they are grilled on both sides.
Arrange them on the plate without sauce.
If you do not have chicken, use other meat such as veal, young rabbit, pheasant, etc.

title: Pieds de Cochon à la Sainte-Menehould (Pig's Feet Sainte-Menehould)
description: Prepared with pig's feet, bay leaf, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Bouillon or water (two tablespoons per pot)
ingredients.sourceText: Bouillon or water (two tablespoons per pot)

steps: Wrap your half pig's feet with wide ribbon or thread so that they do not come apart while cooking.

Place them in a casserole with thyme, bay leaf, carrots, onions, cloves, a bouquet of parsley and chives, a little saltpeter, half a bottle of white wine, and two tablespoons per pot of bouillon or water.
Add a few meat scraps if you have them.
Simmer for twenty-four hours without stopping.
Let them cool in their cooking liquid.
Carefully unwrap them and leave them until the next day.
When you want to prepare them, dip them in warm butter.
Season them with coarse pepper and roll them in breadcrumbs, taking as much as possible.
Place them on a grill over a gentle fire and serve them without sauce.

description: Prepared with cucumbers, vinegar, and chives.
steps: Cut each foot into three pieces after cooking in water and thoroughly cleaning
Cut cucumbers into large pieces and marinate for one hour with one spoonful of vinegar and a little salt
Press them well in your hands to extract all the water
Put them in the saucepan with a piece of butter, a bouquet of parsley, chives, one clove of garlic, half a bay leaf, two cloves

Add a pinch of flour, moistened with bouillon

Add a liaison of egg yolks diluted with cream
Thicken the sauce on the fire without letting it boil, for fear it turns
Before serving, taste if there is enough salt and vinegar, add a little coarse pepper

description: Prepared with bouillon, garlic, and meat.
steps: Cook the feet in water with salt, pepper, laurel leaf, thyme, basil, and garlic for half an hour.
Remove and debone as much as possible.
Prepare the stuffing by chopping a small piece of cooked meat and mixing with beef fat, bread crumbs softened with milk, seasoned with salt, pepper, and chopped parsley and chives.
Bind with three egg yolks and stuff the feet.

To grill: dip in hot butter, coat with bread crumbs, and either grill or bake with a pie cover and coals on top.
Drain off any fat and serve with clean platter edges. Optionally serve with a clear sauce.

description: Prepared with bouillon, verjuice, and onions.
steps: Cook a dozen sheep's feet in water.
Place them in a saucepan with bouillon, a spoonful of verjuice, salt, pepper, some onion slices, a garlic clove, and a carrot cut into zest.
Boil for half an hour to develop flavor.
When well cooked, drain and remove the bones.
Replace each bone with a piece of bread crumb of the same length and thickness.
Fry by passing them on the fire with butter until they achieve a beautiful golden color.
Place a piece in each foot to imitate the removed bone.
Arrange on the serving platter and cover with piquant sauce.

title: Pigeons au Soleil (Pigeons in the Sun)
description: Prepared with pigeons, white wine, and chives.

ingredients.name: white wine for thinning the batter
ingredients.sourceText: white wine for thinning the batter

steps: Have small young pigeons well scalded and emptied; they must retain their wings, head, and feet
Pass a skewer through the thighs of each to prevent them from spreading too much
Blanch them briefly in boiling water
After thoroughly cleaning them, place them in a saucepan with one glass of white wine, a bouquet of parsley, chives, one clove of garlic, two cloves, salt, coarse pepper, and a small piece of butter
When cooked, drain them and let cool, then dip them in a batter and fry until golden
Serve hot with fried parsley around them

For the batter: put two handfuls of flour and fine salt in a saucepan with a little oil, and gradually add white wine to thin the batter until it is neither too thin nor too thick, meaning it should run from the spoon when poured

sourceSteps: Scald and clean the pigeons and cut them in four
Place them in a casserole with one litron of fine peas, one litron for four pigeons
Add a piece of good butter and a bouquet
Pass them over the fire, sprinkle with a pinch of flour, and moisten with bouillon and a little jus
When they are cooked, add a spoonful of coulis, a little sugar the size of a hazelnut, and fine salt
If you have neither jus nor coulis, add a liaison of three egg yolks thinned with a little bouillon
